question: Can a formal constant-F2 sheaf obstruction on an observation cycle and a single noise-calibrated, self-supervised temporal-memory correction infer switching latent defects better or more efficiently than a fully trained HMM and exact Bayesian parity filter?
hypothesis: Pass B, with only one targeted change to Pass A (temporal noise-aware state filtering with transition probability estimated from unlabeled defect changes), should reduce Brier >=20% relative to A on fresh worlds. To establish a unique scientific advantage, it must also improve Brier >=5% versus both a fully trained two-state raw-observation HMM and an exact known-noise/transition Bayesian parity filter (or demonstrate a separately measured >=1.5x whole-process efficiency improvement at equivalent accuracy). Failing strong controls stops tuning this prototype.

predecessor_evidence.note: Previous Stage0 correctly refuted graph-loop-only as a latent-state proof. Formal sheaf construction required.
Prior IPFC bounded two-pass development, isolated and unmerged.

inputs.name: Source-free 3-context triangulated observation cycle with independent per-episode F2 vertex gauges, latent switching obstruction, 10% sensor flips, 24 timesteps/world
inputs.source: Algorithm implemented locally for exploratory A; no original-world data, owner model, native training, protected holdout, or paid API

pass_B.objective: Frozen one-targeted-correction comparison of sheaf defect temporal filter to Pass A, strong trained HMM, known-parameter exact Bayes, and closing-only null.

train.supervised_HMM: Two-state categorical HMM emission model trained with state labels and Laplace smoothing on all eight raw edge symbols; supervised transition MLE
train.SCDR_B: No hidden-state training labels; transition probability derived from unlabeled consecutive obstruction changes and known sensor-noise calibration.

null.h_hidden: Always zero; gauge vectors and sensor noise remain random
null.metric: Rate of false high-confidence h=1 detection at posterior >=0.95

frozen_design.source: CPython 3.12 stdlib, exact deterministic hash-seeded source; source SHA and commit frozen before B first use.
frozen_design.math: Constant F2 cellular sheaf on 3-cycle graph: C0=F2^3, C1=F2^3, d0(x)=(x0 xor x1, x1 xor x2, x2 xor x0), rank(d0)=2, H1=C1/im(d0) dimension1. Defect cohomology representative is XOR of observed three edge measurements. This is true cellular sheaf cohomology, not graph-cycle rank mistaken for it.
frozen_design.generator: At each time t, independent random gauge g0,g1,g2; clean edge observations d0(g) plus one parity obstruction bit h_t; hidden h switches with probability 0.08; each edge sensor independently flips with p=0.10, resulting defect noise q=(1-(1-2p)^3)/2=0.244
frozen_design.matched_budget: All methods receive exactly the same three observed noisy edge bits per time step and temporal stream; no interventions, no external data calls, no owner model.
methods: SCDR_B/one targeted temporal noise-aware self-supervised hidden-state filter
Fully supervised 2-state raw-symbol HMM (strong privileged training-label comparator)
Exact true-parameter Bayesian hidden-state filter on parity (strong privileged oracle comparator)
frozen_design.compute: <=1 CPU minute per platform for source-free fit/evaluation; no GPU or paid services; whole-process cost not separately measured, so no efficiency claim from simple code size.
frozen_design.evaluator: Per-frame hidden obstruction Brier loss primary; threshold .5 accuracy; high-confidence >=0.95 FP/TP; null per-frame confident FP. Report all controls, 96 worlds *24 frames; exact source/result SHA and dual-OS parity.

controls: Fully trained supervised two-state categorical HMM trained on same observation channel (additional labels on training only)
Exact true-parameter Bayesian parity filter (privileged stronger baseline)
No-hidden-state noise-only null to audit spurious defect alarms
metrics: Self-supervised transition estimate vs true rate
Source/result SHA and deterministic two-OS reproducibility

classification_rules.supported: DEVELOPMENT_SIGNAL only if Pass B improves Pass A Brier by >=20%, null confident FP <=5%, and B's Brier/accuracy are within 2% relative Brier and 2pp accuracy of both strongest comparator methods; this supports representation but not scientific superiority. For SCIENCE_CANDIDATE require >=5% Brier gain vs BOTH trained HMM and exact Bayes on same B worlds or verified >=1.5x full-process compute advantage at parity; these stronger claims cannot be made by Stage development alone.
classification_rules.mixed: Pass B improves A but fails strongest HMM/Bayes; DEVELOPMENT_MIXED, stop this implementation after two passes; preserve possible sheaf-invariant feature for independent future work.
classification_rules.negative: Pass B doesn't improve A by 20% or harms noise calibration / accuracy, DEVELOPMENT_NO_GO; stop without third tuning pass.
classification_rules.invalid: Source SHA mismatch, B inspected before source lock, omitted fully trained HMM or exact Bayesian control, label leaked into candidate inference, or post-result retuning/split change invalidates confirmatory development.

prohibited_after_primary_run: tune source based on B results
consume any other original scientific cohort
merge this external experiment into accepted Yggdrasil native learning
claim graph cycle alone proves hidden state
claim stronger sheaf inference than exact Bayes absent evidence
preregistration_note: User requested bounded experimentation (not zero tuning): Pass A smoke failed; only one targeted Pass B memory correction, then continue/pivot/stop. B source to be pinned via separate Git commit before first B execution.
